html:
Lumnanas is an old name, found in Spanish sources, for a people of the northern Gran Chaco, near today's border of Paraguay, Bolivia and Argentina. The map places them west of the Pilcomayo River in the Paraguayan Chaco.

Little reliable information is available on who exactly the name refers to. It is usually tied to the peoples of the Mataco-Mataguayo language family, such as the Chorote, Nivaclé and Wichí. These were hunters, fishers and gatherers who also grew small gardens. Their land was fought over in the Chaco War of 1932 to 1935.
